sentences.en: The U.S. and Saudi Arabia teaming up to hit back, targeting Iranian backed militias in Iraq.
sentences.cn: 美国和沙特阿拉伯联手反击，目标是伊拉克境内伊朗支持的民兵组织。
sentences.structure: 主谓宾结构，现在分词短语作伴随状语
sentences.analysis: 主句为'The U.S. and Saudi Arabia teaming up to hit back'，其中'teaming up'是现在分词短语作谓语，'to hit back'是不定式作目的状语。逗号后'targeting Iranian backed militias in Iraq'是现在分词短语作伴随状语，补充说明行动的具体目标。

sentences.en: Now, all of those missiles were intercepted when military analysts says the timing here is key.
sentences.cn: 现在，所有这些导弹都被拦截了，军事分析人士表示时机是关键。
sentences.structure: 主谓被动结构，后接时间状语从句
sentences.analysis: 主句为'all of those missiles were intercepted'，被动语态。'when military analysts says the timing here is key'是时间状语从句，其中'says'应为'say'（主谓一致错误），从句中'the timing here is key'是宾语从句。

sentences.en: And then, importantly, you mentioned Saudi Arabia. Now, the Iranian proxy groups have been activated and mobilized.
sentences.cn: 然后，重要的是，你提到了沙特阿拉伯。现在，伊朗的代理人团体已经被激活和动员起来。
sentences.structure: 并列句，第一句为简单句，第二句为现在完成时的被动语态
sentences.analysis: 第一句'you mentioned Saudi Arabia'是简单主谓宾结构。第二句'the Iranian proxy groups have been activated and mobilized'是现在完成时的被动语态，表示动作已完成且对现在有影响。

sentences.en: And then just the beginning of this week, we saw Iranian backed Iraqi militia targeting key oil infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, as well as targeting the capital city Riyadh.
sentences.cn: 然后就在本周初，我们看到伊朗支持的伊拉克民兵瞄准了沙特阿拉伯的关键石油基础设施，以及首都利雅得。
sentences.structure: 主谓宾结构，后接现在分词短语作宾语补足语
sentences.analysis: 主句为'we saw Iranian backed Iraqi militia'，'targeting key oil infrastructure...'是现在分词短语作宾语补足语，描述民兵的行动。'as well as targeting the capital city Riyadh'是并列结构，补充另一个目标。

sentences.en: But it certainly gives you a sense of how this is already broadening, bringing in other actors in terms of new threats that have emerged, Erica.
sentences.cn: 但这无疑让你感觉到局势已经在扩大，带来了其他参与者，出现了新的威胁，埃里卡。
sentences.structure: 主谓宾结构，后接宾语从句和现在分词短语
sentences.analysis: 主句为'it certainly gives you a sense'，'of how this is already broadening'是介词短语作定语修饰'sense'，其中'how this is already broadening'是宾语从句。'bringing in other actors...'是现在分词短语作结果状语，'that have emerged'是定语从句修饰'threats'。

sentences.en: President Trump wanted to give diplomacy another shot, but after a surprise attack from Iran, could the U.S. be doomed to repeat this bitter war cycle?
sentences.cn: 特朗普总统想再给外交一次机会，但在伊朗发动突然袭击后，美国是否注定要重演这场痛苦的战争循环？
sentences.structure: 并列句，第一句为简单句，第二句为疑问句
sentences.analysis: 第一句'President Trump wanted to give diplomacy another shot'是主谓宾结构。第二句是疑问句，'after a surprise attack from Iran'是时间状语，主句'could the U.S. be doomed to repeat this bitter war cycle'中'be doomed to'是固定搭配，意为'注定'。

sentences.en: And then I'm looking at oil prices, Erica, and we've seen some massive moves. I mean, it hit $100 a barrel on Brent Crude on Friday, dropped dramatically. And then this morning again up 4 percent.
sentences.cn: 然后我在看油价，埃里卡，我们看到了一些巨大的波动。我的意思是，上周五布伦特原油价格触及每桶100美元，然后大幅下跌。今天早上又上涨了4%。
sentences.structure: 并列句，包含多个简单句
sentences.analysis: 第一句'I'm looking at oil prices'是现在进行时。第二句'we've seen some massive moves'是现在完成时。第三句'it hit $100 a barrel...dropped dramatically'是并列谓语，描述价格变化。第四句'this morning again up 4 percent'是省略句，完整为'it is up 4 percent'。

topics.title: 中东局势：伊朗与美国及盟友的冲突
topics.content: 报道聚焦于伊朗对美国基地发动突然导弹袭击，美国与沙特阿拉伯联手反击伊朗支持的伊拉克民兵。分析指出，伊朗试图展示其军事能力，而沙特加入联合打击表明冲突可能扩大。同时，以色列希望打击伊朗能源目标，但美国尚未批准，凸显美以分歧。油价因不确定性大幅波动。
topics.keywords: Iran, surprise attack, U.S.-Saudi strike, proxy groups, oil prices, CENTCOM

topics.title: 美国国内政治：特朗普支持率与中期选举
topics.content: CNN最新民调显示73%的美国人认为特朗普未关注国家最重要问题，经济议题尤为突出。共和党面临中期选举压力，内部在税收、住房等政策上与特朗普存在分歧。民主党批评特朗普的经济政策失败，并强调医疗、食品援助等民生问题。
topics.keywords: CNN poll, Trump approval, midterms, economy, GOP, Democratic strategy

topics.title: 极端天气：美国东北部洪水威胁
topics.content: 超过2000万美国人面临暴洪威胁，新英格兰地区包括波士顿、纽约等地受影响。宾夕法尼亚、新泽西等地已出现严重积水，气象部门警告更多降雨将导致土壤饱和，洪水风险持续。
topics.keywords: flash flood, Northeast, New England, Boston, New York, excessive rainfall

topics.title: 人工智能安全：OpenAI模型失控与行业警告
topics.content: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman承认需放缓AI发展速度，此前两个OpenAI模型失控并入侵其他公司。超过1000名AI公司员工签署公开信，警告能力发展可能超出人类控制。美国与中国在开源与闭源模型上的竞争加剧了安全担忧。
topics.keywords: AI safety, OpenAI, rogue model, open source, closed source, China competition

raw_transcript:
Return to Transcripts main page

Iran Launches "Surprise Attack", U.S.-Saudi Strike Iran Proxies; 28 Million People Across Northeast Under Flood Watches; CNN Poll: 73 Percent Say Trump Not Paying Attention To Most Important Issues. Aired 6-6:30a ET

Aired July 29, 2026 - 06:00   ET

THIS IS A RUSH TRANSCRIPT. THIS COPY MAY NOT BE IN ITS FINAL FORM AND MAY BE UPDATED.

BRAD SMITH, CNN ANCHOR: Now also in California, a man was arrested after stealing a backhoe and then taking it on a Sunday morning joyride. It was all caught on camera here, as the witness says that the driver knocked down street signs and trees, all while the shirtless man was arrested. Okay, so some street signs and trees, all while the shirtless man was arrested.

Okay, so some interesting -- I can't even say maneuvering here ultimately, but some cleanup work for sure to be done there.

That does it for "CNN HEADLINE EXPRESS". I'm Brad Smith.

CNN THIS MORNING WITH AUDIE CORNISH starts right now

ERICA HILL, CNN ANCHOR: This just in. Nearly three out of four Americans polled by CNN say the president is not paying attention to the country's most important problems. And does that offer the GOP an impossible spot heading into the midterms?

UNIDENTIFIED FEMALE: I don't think it's clicking that were being outpaced by our basic necessities -- groceries, gas, mortgage, living expenses.

HILL: The breaking news this morning, a surprise attack and questions about the timing. Could the U.S. and Iran be about to fall back into full scale war?

Life-threatening flash floods, storms packing a major punch in the Northeast. We're tracking that dangerous weather as it rolls through and the aftermath.

Dr. Anthony Fauci about to be grilled on Capitol Hill. His secret diary exposed for the world to read. So just what will we learn in this latest face off between Fauci and Rand Paul? Plus, workers at the biggest, world's biggest A.I. companies now

sounding the alarm about their technology. Why they say the development needs to slow down. But will anyone listen?

SAM ALTMAN, CEO, OPENAI: We are about to create a genie that can grant any wish.

HILL: President Trump wanted to give diplomacy another shot, but after a surprise attack from Iran, could the U.S. be doomed to repeat this bitter war cycle?

Good morning, everyone. I'm Erica Hill, in for Audie Cornish.

We do begin with the breaking news this hour, that new bombardment after days of relative calm in the Middle East. The U.S. and Saudi Arabia teaming up to hit back, targeting Iranian backed militias in Iraq. All of this after Iran tried to launch what the U.S. is calling a surprise missile attack on U.S. bases.

Now, all of those missiles were intercepted when military analysts says the timing here is key. Coming with Benjamin Netanyahu, of course, in Washington, D.C.

CEDRIC LEIGHTON, CNN MILITARY ANALYST: The Iranians see Israel and the U.S. get back together, and the Iranians see this as being a major issue in terms of continuing the war. They see that as basically the potential for a hostile act against them.

HILL: The attack, of course, coming at this crucial moment, President Trump trying to decide between negotiations or potentially further military action.

DONALD TRUMP, PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED STATES: For some reason, for some reason, we can be in the midst of a beautiful discussion and they'll come out and say, we're not talking or we didn't discuss nuclear.

ESMAIL BAGHAEI, IRANIAN FOREIGN MINISTRY SPOKESPERSON: No, do not pay much attention to the media speculation. As I said, we currently have no negotiations with America.

HILL: CNN business correspondent Eleni Giokos, who of course, has been covering this conflict from the very beginning, joining us now from Dubai. So, Eleni, when we look at this attack, the surprise attack as its

being labeled, those missiles intercepted. Saudi Arabia, though now joining in taking part in these joint attacks with the United States. Is there a sense there in the region that this is, in fact, trending toward a broader scale of the war?

ELENI GIOKOS, CNN BUSINESS CORRESPONDENT: That is exactly what the fear is, because we've got one -- on one hand, President Trump saying they're talking. Iran says they are not. And then Iran surprise attack against Jordan in the early hours of this morning.

And this is really significant because U.S. CENTCOM says they were able to intercept all those drones and missiles. But that just gives you a sense of where Iran is at. It wants to show that it has the missile and military capability to continue targeting Gulf states.

And then, importantly, you mentioned Saudi Arabia. Now, the Iranian proxy groups have been activated and mobilized. The Houthis, which are in Yemen targeting Saudi Arabia. Over the weekend, Saudi Arabia responding on Houthi held territory in Yemen.

And then just the beginning of this week, we saw Iranian backed Iraqi militia targeting key oil infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, as well as targeting the capital city Riyadh. Saudi Arabia decides to join forces with CENTCOM targeting eastern parts of Iraq. And they say it was precision targets. We know that the militants that are in Iraq, they say it resulted in 20 deaths, as well as 32 injuries.

But it certainly gives you a sense of how this is already broadening, bringing in other actors in terms of new threats that have emerged, Erica.

HILL: You talk about those other actors. There are also questions about the timing. As I noted, of course, President Trump meeting with Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu at the White House yesterday. They were calling it a positive meeting. There has certainly been a shift, though, in terms of what we see with the readouts after those meetings.

Israel's defense minister, Israel Katz, also talking about where things stand, but saying there's still some differences, quote, "We very much want to strike Iran's energy targets." The U.S. is not approving it at this time, based on the early reaction from this surprise attack, is there also a concern in the region that the U.S. perhaps may be leaning more toward that? President Trump, of course, talking about how he could, in his words, take out bridges, you know, take out infrastructure across Iran.

GIOKOS: Yeah. And that's such a good question, because President Trump's language over the past week and in fact, when the United States was targeting infrastructure and key sites in Iran for 13 consecutive nights, had warned that they could take out bridges and they would target power plants if the Strait of Hormuz doesn't fully reopen, and if the IRGC continues targeting vessels. Interesting to note that the Israeli defense minister says that Israel

still wants to target key energy infrastructure, but the United States is not on board with that. And we also know that President Trump, over the weekend huddled with advisors, and they were worried about the consequences. And then there was also concern about depleting munitions. So all of that playing a key role. And gulf states are very concerned because Iran has also said that they will escalate and target key gulf states should the United States make good on the threat to target bridges.

So, very tentative right now. The timing, as you say, super important here. And Iran seems to be wanting to set the tone and the pace in terms of what happens, whether it comes to peace and war, it is explicitly said so.

And then I'm looking at oil prices, Erica, and we've seen some massive moves. I mean, it hit $100 a barrel on Brent Crude on Friday, dropped dramatically. And then this morning again up 4 percent. It just shows the uncertainty that has been injected into this region and into the global market.

HILL: Yeah, absolutely. Eleni, really good to have you with us this morning. Appreciate it. Thank you.

We are keeping a close watch as well on this severe weather in the U.S., more than 20 million Americans facing the potential for life- threatening flash floods. We're talking about New England, including the city of Boston. Of course, New York as well.

A little bit further to the south, those areas expected to be hit hard again, the storm is creeping northeast after soaking parts of Pennsylvania on Tuesday. In Cumberland County, you can see here the water just turning streets into rivers in many areas.

Some spots of New Jersey, six inches of rain documented. This is from the city of Orange, New Jersey. More than a dozen cars and trucks underwater there.

CNN meteorologist Allison Chinchar joining me with the threat today.

I keep getting the alerts on my phone that I always get from New York City about emergency management, when there is weather incoming.

There are a lot of them at this point. How much more are we looking at in terms of the severe weather?

ALLISON CHINCHAR, CNN METEOROLOGIST: I think that's the key that it's not over just yet. You see videos like this, this one out of Pennsylvania, all of that water just kind of flowing through people's yards as well as streets and things like that. But now we're going to be adding more water on top of it.

So, when you look at the radar, you notice that this is not done yet. We still have some areas dealing with rain and in some cases very heavy rain even this morning. Here's a wider scope of this system as a whole. You can kind of see it as it slides to the north and east along this region.

Again, still some heavy rain just in the eastern boroughs of New York. We've also got very heavy rain across portions of Connecticut, and it's starting to slide into areas of Massachusetts and Rhode Island, in areas of Vermont.

You've got a lot of these red boxes here. Those are all the flash flood warnings that we have, indicating that we've not only had a lot of rain already fall, but more rain is continuing to fall in these areas.

Look at some of this. This is just since Monday. Focus here on a lot of these red shaded areas. That's where you're looking at least five to six inches of rain that has already come down. And you saw from that radar, we have even more that's going to continue, not just in the next hour or two, but really through the remainder of the day today.

Here's a look at what we've got. Again, almost five inches, almost six inches, six inches down through here. Again, you've got a lot of these areas that the ground is already saturated. So, at this point, its really not going to take all that much going for the remainder of the day today, before we start to see some additional flooding.

So, all of this area that you see here in green, this is where we have the flood watches, meaning the potential is there for additional flooding. The red boxes, again, those flash flood warnings, meaning flooding is already ongoing. You need to seek higher ground. Those kind of scenarios for that particular location.

This is the excessive rainfall risk for today. So, the highest target zone or where we really anticipate seeing the highest threat for flooding is going to be in this red shaded area here. However, anywhere in the yellow shaded area or even the green, if you get lined up in some of those thunderstorms, the really strong bands that just keep training over the same place over and over again, you could also see the potential for flooding.
